extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers of clinical and translational research manuscripts (medical researchers, clinicians, academic reviewers)
extracted.subtask_short: peer review of clinical research manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing thorough, unbiased, and constructive peer review of clinical and translational research manuscripts, covering core principles, section-by-section assessment, practical best practices, and reviewer responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must disclose any potential conflicts of interest, including financial, professional, or personal biases that could affect their impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maintain transparency and protect the integrity of the process, reviewers should disclose conflicts to editors so appropriate steps (e.g., recusal) can be taken; undisclosed conflicts constitute unacceptable deviation from impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must have sufficient knowledge in the manuscript’s subject area to provide a useful assessment of its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expertise ensures reviewers can evaluate scientific rigor, relevance, and quality appropriately; if lacking expertise, reviewers should decline the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback should highlight strengths and weaknesses and provide actionable recommendations for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be specific, feasible, and aimed at improving clarity, methodological robustness, or interpretative accuracy; maintain a clear and constructive tone and avoid unhelpful or dismissive remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of data and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must meticulously examine the data and confirm that the conclusions drawn are well-supported by the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot incomplete or inadequate results and particularly overinterpretation in the Discussion; identify gaps or inconsistencies in data reporting that could undermine findings; ensure conclusions are proportionate to the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of data integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically assess whether the data are presented consistently, accurately, and without apparent fabrication or manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for internal inconsistencies, missing data, inappropriate data handling, and whether supplementary data support claims; raise concerns to editors when integrity issues are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of novelty and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the uniqueness of the findings and the value they add to existing knowledge as well as potential influence on clinical practice, policy, or future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work advances the field enough to warrant publication; weigh originality alongside methodological quality when forming a recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the study design is appropriate for the research question and that methods are statistically and technically correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check adequacy of sample sizes, correctness of statistical analyses, appropriateness of controls, and whether methods provide reproducible, testable procedures; request detailed methods or analyses if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of improvement areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific suggestions for improving the manuscript’s clarity, methods, analyses, and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions should be feasible and practical (e.g., data visualization, clarification of argument, additional analyses); if a requested improvement cannot be incorporated, advise that limitation be discussed explicitly in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of relevance (originality and significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the research is novel and significant enough to warrant publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind the potential to advance the field; relevance should be a paramount consideration across all papers reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial evaluations (avoidance of bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be based solely on scientific content and not influenced by author institution, reputation, nationality, or other non-scientific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unbiased assessment is essential; strategies to mitigate bias include training and (where appropriate) blinded review; disclose if impartiality cannot be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the title accurately reflects the study content and the abstract provides a concise, standalone summary of the question, methods, results, and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest concise, expressive titles and discourage long, discursive titles; ensure abstract is self-contained and faithful to the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the Introduction establishes background, rationale, and clearly outlines the study’s purpose with appropriate citation of relevant literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the literature review is adequate and that the research question or hypothesis is clearly stated and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: ethical soundness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify ethical approval/consent where applicable, appropriateness of the methodology, adequacy of statistical approach, and that sufficient detail is provided for reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major role of Methods is to ensure the work/analysis can be reproduced at independent centers; reviewers should look for detailed, complete, and retrievable information in the manuscript or supplementary appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: transparency and non-redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure results are presented transparently and unambiguously and are consistent with study objectives; avoid unnecessary repetition between text and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tables contain extensive details, Results text should summarize and refer to tables for details; criticize redundant repetition and ask for clearer presentation where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: interpretation, limitations, and proportionate conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate accuracy of interpretation, whether alternative explanations are considered, and whether study limitations are acknowledged; ensure conclusions are proportionate to the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for overinterpretation and that authors discuss limitations; recommend tempering conclusions that exceed what data support and inclusion of alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables: stand-alone clarity and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual elements should be understandable without referring back to the text and should include definitions of abbreviations for each figure/table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify accuracy, non-redundancy, alignment with content, and legibility (e.g., appropriate font sizes); request that abbreviations be defined in each table/figure legend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with journal-specific features and requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must adhere to the journal’s instructions to authors regarding writing, graphics, and formatting conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check items such as definition of abbreviations at first mention, legible fonts in tables/figures, referenced style requirements, and flag noncompliance to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism, tone and respectfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a professional, respectful, and constructive tone throughout the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality reviews require clarity and respect; avoid ad hominem or dismissive language and focus critique on the science and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete reviews within a reasonable timeframe, suggested as 10–14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reviews facilitate prompt editorial decisions and rapid dissemination of important findings; decline or request an extension if unable to meet timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of suggested improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for improvement should be realistic and implementable within the scope of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid recommending unrealistic experiments or extensive new studies as mandatory changes; if certain improvements are infeasible, recommend authors acknowledge them as limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutiny of supplementary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully examine supplementary material to ensure it provides necessary details for reproducibility and supports claims in the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure supplementary tables/appendices include retrievable methods, raw data, or code where required; request missing supplementary information when reproducibility is impeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation clarity (decision guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based solely on manuscript quality, reviewers should provide clear recommendations (e.g., minor revisions, major revisions, rejection) guided by the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should be justified by the review’s findings on rigor, novelty, impact, and compliance; avoid letting journal prestige or author identity influence recommendation.
